title: Five idle children's hospitals to open in December after 1,440 posts created
excerpt: The hospitals in Rajshahi, Khulna, Rangpur, Barishal and Cumilla stood unused for one to six years after construction. Not all posts have been filled yet.

image.alt: Rangpur Medical College campus in Rangpur, one of the cities getting a children's hospital
image.credit: File photo: Mahtabb / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0

content:
Five specialised children's hospitals that stood unused for years after their buildings were finished will open in the second week of December, when Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is due to inaugurate them, Prothom Alo reported on Thursday (26 November).

The hospitals are in Rajshahi, Khulna (divisional), Rangpur, Barishal and Cumilla. According to Prothom Alo, they could not start services because of a lack of staff, equipment and administrative approval, although some offered limited care as part of other hospitals. Prothom Alo's lead report on 12 April said six children's hospital buildings had been lying idle for one to six years. The six buildings cost Tk 320 crore and have 1,050 beds in total.

Dr SM Ziauddin Haider, the Prime Minister's special assistant on health, told Prothom Alo on Wednesday that the hospitals were ready to open. The state news agency BSS reported that 1,440 posts have been created for them, including 100 senior consultants, 200 junior consultants and 325 medical officers, and that deputy directors appointed to the five hospitals have been told to join by 29 November. Haider said not all posts had been filled yet but appointments would follow.

According to BSS, equipment including neonatal ventilators, CT scanners, X-ray machines, cardiac monitors and phototherapy machines has been delivered. Rangpur's civil surgeon, Dr Shaheen Sultana, told Prothom Alo she had heard some equipment had arrived but had not seen it.

The sixth hospital, in Sylhet, is a general hospital and will open under Sylhet Medical University, its vice-chancellor told the newspaper. Public health expert Dr Mushtaq Hossain said divisional children's hospitals were useful but often opened without full equipment or staff, and should gradually become general hospitals that also offer maternal care.

Why it matters

Dengue and measles are pushing up child admissions, and paediatric and ICU beds are hard to find outside Dhaka. If staffed, the hospitals could ease pressure on medical college hospitals. NGOs referring sick children from districts in these divisions will need to know which services actually start in December.

What to watch

  • The inauguration date and which services open on day one.
  • How many of the 1,440 posts are filled, especially specialists and nurses.
  • Whether ICU and neonatal care start, or only outpatient services.

Sources
